correctness.rationale: Writing \(q=\mathcal R_0^2\), the source formula makes \(q\) the larger root of \(q^2-Sq+P=0\). If \(S>2\), then \(q\ge S/2>1\). If \(S\le2\), the larger root exceeds one exactly when the quadratic at one is negative, namely \(1-S+P<0\). This proves the two-branch criterion. For the package's exact example, \(S=P=16/3\), the discriminant is \(64/9\) and the larger root is exactly four, while \(S-P-1=-1\). The inspected exact-rational verifier reconstructs the six transmission rates from admissible primitive parameters and checks every equilibrium residual at the displayed one-half state is zero.

value.rationale: The basic reproduction threshold controls local disease-free stability and is then used in the article's endemic-equilibrium discussion. Missing an entire supercritical branch is a substantive qualitative error; the exact criterion and admissible counterexample directly repair the model analysis.

final_claim: For the autonomous Oropouche next-generation formula with \(S=R_{FA}+R_{FH}+R_{CH}\) and \(P=R_{FA}R_{CH}\), the exact supercritical criterion is \(\mathcal R_0>1\) if and only if \(S>2\) or \(P<S-1\). Thus the appendix criterion \(P<S-1\) misses a genuine supercritical branch; the explicit admissible parameter point in RESULT.md has \(S=P=16/3\), \(\mathcal R_0^2=4\), violates the appendix inequality, and possesses the displayed positive endemic equilibrium.
limitations: This corrects the autonomous threshold/equilibrium criterion in the cited Oropouche model; it does not re-evaluate the paper's seasonal data-fitting conclusions.
